A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MMAD and the same MMA-52 dataset, and all supplied pages are readable. Neither contains an appendix, although v2 Section 5.1 refers to one for implementation details. This missing material limits comparison of experimental documentation.

before.justification: v1 Table 3 reports original MMA-52 detection experiments with MS-TCT and PointTAD.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments, DSTA results, adapter ablations, error analyses, and qualitative predictions in Tables 3–5 and Figures 6–8.

M1.justification: v1 evaluates existing detectors without proposing a detection algorithm. v2 introduces DSTA: parallel spatial and temporal depthwise-convolution paths with learnable fusion weights, incorporated into an adapter-based detection pipeline (Section 4.3). This is a substantive new method.

E1.justification: MMA-52 retains its 6,528 videos, 19,782 instances, 203 subjects, and 52 action categories. v2 adds explicit evaluation at seven body-level categories alongside action-level detection. Other datasets discussed in its expanded comparisons are not additional evaluated benchmarks.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains MS-TCT and PointTAD and adds ActionFormer, TemporalMaxer, TriDet, DyFadet, TadTR, Re2TAL, AdaTAD, and a row labeled VideoMamba. Table 4 also compares fine-tuning and adapter alternatives. The VideoMamba row's reference [57] identifies an unrelated gait-analysis review, leaving that comparator's attribution unclear.

E3.justification: The cross-subject splits and 0.1–0.9 tIoU averaging remain unchanged. v2 adds body-level evaluation and a combined hierarchical average, experiments with multiple backbone configurations, controlled adapter comparisons, and error profiling at tIoU 0.5 with coverage, duration, and instance-count buckets. These expand the evaluation design without establishing that the original baseline settings changed.

E4.justification: v2 adds adapter-choice and fusion-weight ablations (Tables 4–5), false-positive and false-negative diagnostics (Figures 6–7), and prediction case studies (Figure 8). These test component effectiveness and failure conditions absent from v1. Dataset analysis also gains duration variability, while v1's splitwise temporal-density analysis is absent from the supplied v2.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 4 newly reports action-duration means with standard deviations at action and body levels. This describes dataset variability, not uncertainty across model runs. Neither supplied PDF reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Shared MS-TCT and PointTAD action-level entries remain unchanged, including averages of 3.51 and 4.51. v2 adds extensive comparator, body-level, ablation, and diagnostic results; DSTA-B reports 20.30 action-level, 30.37 body-level, and 25.34 combined mAP. Its main table no longer lists six original threshold-specific columns. These are expanded results, not improvements to the retained baseline scores.

T1.justification: The set-prediction formulation remains substantively equivalent. v2 adds mathematical definitions of adapter transformations, including DSTA's weighted spatial/temporal fusion in Equation 3. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The MMAD task and MMA-52 dataset contributions remain. v2's abstract, introduction, and conclusion additionally claim a proposed DSTA solution and experimental validation of its effectiveness. This changes the paper from a dataset introduction with preliminary baselines into a dataset-and-method contribution.

C2.justification: v1 mainly concludes that PointTAD performs better and substantial improvement remains possible. v2 adds explanations involving spatial information, category imbalance, hierarchical variability, and failures on short, low-coverage, densely occurring actions. Some interpretations are inconsistent: Section 5.4 calls background errors predominant, whereas Figure 6 and its caption emphasize confusion and wrong-label errors.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents clip construction, annotator training, independent annotation and cross-checking, plus OpenTAD, mixed precision, checkpointing, frame resolution, and adapter learning rates. v1's detailed MS-TCT/PointTAD hyperparameters are not reproduced in the supplied v2 main text; the missing referenced appendix prevents determining whether those details were relocated.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantial related-work discussions covering micro-action recognition, temporal detection, and adapter methods. Its dataset comparison shifts from MultiTHUMOS/Charades toward micro-action datasets, hierarchical labels, and availability. DSTA is explicitly positioned against AdaTAD's temporal-only adaptation, materially expanding the research positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten around micro-action characteristics and explicit contributions. Dataset discussion is reorganized into construction, properties, and comparison; the problem formulation moves into a dedicated methodology section, and experiments gain separate analysis subsections. Author and affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, substantially redesigns dataset illustrations and distribution plots, and introduces an adapter schematic, duration plot, diagnostic figures, and prediction visualizations. Table 3 gains grouped methods, backbone information, and hierarchical metric columns; Tables 4–5 add ablation displays.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the benchmark's evidential value: annotation procedures become assessable, broader detector comparisons better establish achievable performance, and ablations and diagnostics identify specific failure modes beyond v1's preliminary results. These gains outweigh material reporting weaknesses. The referenced implementation appendix is missing, Section 5.2 states AdaTAD's best average as 21.08 although Table 3 gives 23.08, and the Figure 6 discussion is inconsistent with the plot; these issues still limit reproducibility and confidence in some interpretations.
